Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice E.S.Indiresh
 Oral Judgment

These appeals are arising out of the judgment and award dated 17.02.2020 in MVC No.645/2013, on the file of Senior Civil Judge and Additional MACT at Basavakalyan (hereinafter referred to as 'Tribunal'), awarding compensation to the claimant.
2. For the sake of brevity, the parties in the appeal shall be referred to in terms of their status and ranking before the Tribunal.
3. It is the case of the claimant that, the claimant was working as a cleaner in the lorry bearing registration No.MH-25/B-9428, belonging to respondent No.1.

On 12.11.2012, the driver of the lorry was proceeding towards Hyderabad and when the vehicle in question NC: 2026:KHC-K:889 HC-KAR reached near RTO check-post of Zaheerabad on NH-9, the driver of the lorry bearing registration No.MH-25/B-9428, drover the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the backside of another lorry bearing registration No.AP-16/TK-1046 and as a result of the same, the claimant sustained grievous injuries.
Hence, the claimant has filed MVC No.645/2013 seeking compensation.
4. The claim petition was contested by the respondents therein on merits.
In order to establish their case, the claimant has examined two witnesses as PW.1 and PW.2 and got marked 13 documents and the same were marked as Exs.P1 to P13.
The respondents have examined two witnesses as RW.1 and RW.2 and got marked three documents and the same were marked as Exs.R1 to R3.

The Tribunal after considering the material on record, by judgment and award dated 17.02.2020 allowed the claim petition in part and being aggrieved by the same, the Insurance Company has preferred MFA NC: 2026:KHC-K:889 HC-KAR No.200076/2021 challenging liability as well as quantum and the claimant as filed MFA No.201568/2020 seeking enhancement of compensation.
5. Heard Sri Subhash Mallapur, the learned counsel appearing for the appellant - Insurance Company and Sri Sanjeevkumar C. Patil, the learned counsel appearing for the appellant - claimant.

sentences.text: It is argued by Sri Subhash Mallapur, the learned counsel appearing for the appellant - Insurance Company that, the claim petition is not maintainable for non-joinder of necessary parties, as the claimant has not made the owner and insurer of the lorry as the parties to the proceedings.

It is also argued by the learned counsel appearing for the appellant that, the alleged accident occurred on account of lorry, which has been parked in the middle of the road and therefore, the Tribunal has committed an error in entertaining the claim petition.

It is also contended by the learned counsel appearing for the appellant that, as per Ex.P11, no premium has been NC: 2026:KHC-K:889 HC-KAR collected by the appellant - insurance Company for the cleaner and there is no coverage in the policy in question and therefore, sought for interference of this Court.

7. Per contra, Sri Sanjeevkumar C. Patil, the learned counsel appearing for the claimant sought to justify the impugned judgment and award regarding liability, however, sought for enhancement of compensation.

8. In the light of the submission made by learned counsel appearing for the parties, the case of the claimant that, the driver of respondent No.1 was charge sheeted and therefore, the contention of the learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company that, the claim petition is not maintainable for non-joinder of parties cannot be accepted.
Perusal of the police records and the spot panchanama would indicate that, the driver of respondent No.1 was negligent and therefore, the alleged accident occurred.

It is also to be noted that, as Ex.R2 - policy do not cover the cleaner and therefore, it is violation NC: 2026:KHC-K:889 HC-KAR of the terms and conditions of the policy and therefore, the appellant - Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation to the claimant and thereafter, recover the same from the owner of the vehicle in question.
9. Insofar as award of compensation is concerned, the injuries sustained by the claimant, as per Exs.P4 and P8 makes it clear that, the claimant has sustained grievous injuries and therefore, the disability is assessed at 22%.

As the accident is of the year 2012, as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, monthly income of the claimant is to be taken at Rs.6,500/- and by applying the multiplier 17, the compensation towards loss of earning capacity would be Rs.2,91,720/- (Rs.6,500x12x17x22%).

Taking into account the grievous injuries sustained by the claimant as per Exs.P4 and P8 as well the evidence of treating doctor (PW.2), the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is reassessed as follows:
NC: 2026:KHC-K:889 HC-KAR Heads Amount Pain and suffering Rs.1,00,000/-
Loss of earnings during laid up Rs.19,500/-
period (Rs.6,500x3)
Loss of amenities Rs.1,00,000/-
Loss of future of earnings Rs.2,91,720/-
Towards
attendant charges Rs.20,000/-

Towards diet and conveyance Rs.20,000/-

Thus, the clamant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.1,08,300/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum.

10. In the result, I pass the following:
ORDER I.
The appeal filed the appellant/Insurance Company in MFA No.200076/2021 is hereby dismissed.
NC: 2026:KHC-K:889 HC-KAR II.
The appeal filed by the appellant/claimant in MFA No.201568/2022 is hereby allowed in part.

III. The appellant/claimant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.1,08,300/- with interest at the rate of 6%
per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.

IV. The appellant - Insurance Company is directed to pay the said compensation to the claimant within a period six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment and thereafter, recover the same from the owner of the vehicle in question.
V. The amount in deposit, if any, be transmitted to the Tribunal.
